name: שִׁמְרִי
summary: Four men, all in Chronicles: an ancestor of Ziza, a prince of Simeon (1Ch 4:37); the father of Jediael and Joha, two of David's mighty men (1Ch 11:45); a Merarite gatekeeper, son of Hosah, whom his father made chief though he was not the firstborn (1Ch 26:10); and a Levite of the sons of Elizaphan who helped cleanse the house of Yahweh under Hezekiah (2Ch 29:13). The name is the root שמר with the ending ‑î: either “my keeping, my watch”, or a short form of a name like Shemariah, “Yahweh has kept”. Scripture does not explain it. Two of the four are Levites, whose work was “to keep the charge” of the house (Num 3:7), and one of them a gatekeeper.

evidence.note: “Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: שִׁמְרִי the chief, for he was not the firstborn, but his father made him chief”: among the gatekeepers.
“Of the sons of Elizaphan, שִׁמְרִי and Jeuel”, among the Levites who cleansed the house.
“Ziza son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of שִׁמְרִי, son of Shemaiah.”
“Jediael son of שִׁמְרִי, and Joha his brother, the Tizite.”
The Levites' work, in the root's words: וְשָׁמְרוּ אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ, “they shall keep his charge”.

note: The ‑î may be the first-person suffix, an adjectival ending, or the remnant of a divine name; scripture gives no ground to choose.
